description: My project, Pass It On, lets the machines NASA left on the Moon and Mars tell their own stories to kids aged 9-13. Surveyor 3, the Apollo 12 science station, the Apollo 15 moon buggy, the Viking landers, Sojourner, and Spirit and Opportunity. Kids can say "Hey Quill" to pause a film and ask a question, and every answer comes from NASA facts with its source. Interests: storytelling, education, web development and space exploration.
summary: Pass It On is a voice-driven story website where six machines NASA left on the Moon and Mars tell their own stories to kids aged 9-13. Surveyor 3, the Apollo 12 science station, the Apollo 15 moon buggy, the Viking landers, Sojourner, and Spirit and Opportunity each star in a three-minute animated film, guided by Quill, a rookie astronaut about to launch. Each film shows who built the machine, how it got there, how its mission worked, what it found and why it stayed, with real NASA photos throughout. Kids can interrupt at any time by saying "Hey Quill" or typing a question: the film pauses, the machine answers in its own voice using only NASA facts, shows its NASA source, and then carries on. This answers the challenge by turning dense archive records into true, first-person stories that connect each machine's engineering to the science it made possible. It matters because these forgotten machines laid the foundations for Artemis and Perseverance, and the next explorers are today's kids.
details:
🌕 Details

Pass It On turns NASA's records about abandoned hardware into stories kids can watch, question and trust. Quill, a rookie astronaut, visits six machines: three on the Moon and three on Mars. Each one tells its story in eight chapters: who I am, why NASA sent me, who built me and what I cost, how I got there, my parts, how my mission worked, what I found, and why I stayed. Each machine passes one lesson into Quill's kit, and with all six, Quill launches toward the next frontier.

🎙️ How It Works

  • The films are animated videos drawn in code and voiced with ElevenLabs, with captions that light up word by word.
  • Saying "Hey Quill" (or typing) pauses the film, and the machine answers in its own voice.
  • Answers come from Qwen3 235B on Amazon Bedrock, which only gets that machine's NASA facts plus NASA fact sheets for Earth, the Moon and Mars. It must use only those numbers, say "I'm not sure" when the facts don't say, and show its NASA source.
  • "I don't get it" retells the current line in simpler words.

💻 Tech Stack

  • React 19, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS
  • Web Speech API for "Hey Quill"
  • ElevenLabs Text to Speech for the narration (with word timings) and live answers
  • Qwen3 235B on Amazon Bedrock for answers
  • Google Gemini image generation for the painted backgrounds
  • Vercel for hosting and server functions
  • Code: https://github.com/SHIVANI-PONTURU/Pass-It-On-

✨ Innovation Highlights

📖 Told by the machines: each one speaks in the first person and passes on a real lesson.

🗣️ Kids talk back: they can interrupt any film and ask anything, by voice or typing.

📡 Data trust: every film line shows its NASA source on screen, and every answer links to one.

🏷️ Real vs AI made clear: every picture is labelled Real photo, Diagram, Model or AI illustration.

🧪 Results

  • 8 of 8 test questions answered with a NASA source, in 1.1 seconds on average.
  • 7 of 8 answers fully correct against the NASA facts; the one slip (the Moon's night temperature used for Mars) is the next fix.
  • "Hey Quill" never went off by mistake across 204 spoken lines.

♿ Accessibility and Privacy

Captions are always on, every voice action also has a button or text box, and it works with a keyboard and screen readers, with reduced motion and no flashing. There are no accounts or tracking, and questions are not stored.
